title: Quarterly Health — Metric Glossary & KPI Tables (Customer Success Draft)
summary: Working draft of canonical metric definitions we should use in QBR decks and renewal conversations. Includes: practical formulas, measurement windows, example targets by customer tier, alert triggers, a plain-text KPI table, and renewal-tracker field suggestions. Intended for CS + SRE + Solutions to align on what we put in executive slides. NOT final — open questions flagged at the bottom.
metric_definitions:
Latency (generation) — What: time between server receive and final token emitted (ms). Formula: response_end_ts - request_start_ts. Prefer generation-only (exclude client-side/network when possible). Windows: rolling 30d and 7d. Percentiles tracked: p50, p95, p99. Sources: Redwood Console traces / per-request telemetry (primary), Prometheus histograms (secondary). Typical targets: enterprise p95 < 300ms, standard p95 < 600ms, freemium p95 < 1200ms. Alerts: p95 increases >20% WoW OR p99 > 1200ms for 1h. Notes: annotate any model changes / rollout windows — latency bumps during rollouts are expected.

Uptime (service and model) — What: % successful request windows excluding scheduled maintenance. Two flavors: service availability (API endpoint responding) and model availability (model has capacity and is not degraded). Formula (service): (total_time - downtime) / total_time * 100. Measurement window: calendar month (to match SLAs) and 30d rolling for operational view. Sources: healthcheck pings, load-balancer 5xx logs, SLO engine. Targets: enterprise SLA 99.95% monthly, standard 99.9%. Alerts: any partial outage impacting >1% of requests for >15 minutes.

Cost / token — What: realized spend per generated token. Formula: total_inference_spend / total_tokens_generated (USD/token or USD/1k tokens). Data: billing export + token counts from request logs. Window: monthly and trailing 90d. Targets: show baseline and desired delta (e.g., reduce by 10–30% by batching/quantization). Alerts: cost/token rising >15% MoM with usage growth >10%.

Cache hit rate — What: fraction of requests resolved from a cache (prefix or KV) vs total cacheable lookups. Formula: cache_hits / cache_lookups. Sources: runtime metrics (cache.* counters), Redwood Console cache dashboard. Window: 7d and 30d. Targets: workload-dependent; recommended baseline: >=70% for repeatable, prompt-stable workloads. Alerts: hit rate drops >15% WoW or absolute <40% for >24h. Notes: low hit rate often due to customer-side prompt variability (dynamic context, timestamps) — recommend prefix canonicalization and TTL tuning.

-- | -- | -- | -- | -- | --

Uptime (service) | % of time endpoints healthy | Healthchecks / LB logs | Monthly / 30d | E: 99.95% / S: 99.9% / F: 99% | Any outage >15m impacting >1% of traffic

Avg tokens per request | tokens generated per request | Request logs | 30d | Used for cost modelling | Sudden drift >25% WoW (investigate prompts)
playbook_actions:
If latency regresses: 1) Check recent model rollouts and canary config (Console -> Rollouts). 2) Verify autoscaling and queue depth (SRE). 3) Temporarily route to fallback model variant with same semantic if needed. 4) Ask customer for sample requests (obfuscate PII) to inspect KV cacheability.

If uptime incident: 1) Triage with runbook: identify service vs model-level issue. 2) If model unavailable, failover to alternative region or lower-capacity pool. 3) Notify CS escalation contact and update incident timeline in Jira.

If cost/token spikes: 1) Confirm billing (billing export) and token accounting. 2) Check for prompt drift (look at avg tokens/request). 3) Recommend batching or quantization profile (Ops/Infra). 4) Run experiment with caching TTL/better prefixing for high-volume endpoints.

If cache hit rate low: 1) Verify that requests are cacheable (static system prompts, no timestamps). 2) Propose prompt canonicalization with Solutions Eng. 3) Tune TTLs and increase prefix cache coverage. 4) Set measurement goal and A/B test changes for 2 weeks.
qbr_template:
QBR slide order (short):
1) Title + top-line health score (green/yellow/red)
2) Exec summary: 30s pitch on adoption, cost trend, renewal risk
3) Metric snapshot: table with p50/p95 latency, uptime, cost/1k, cache hit rate (30d)
4) Trend charts: 90d charts for each metric with annotations (deploys, capacity changes)
5) Incidents & mitigations in quarter
6) Optimization opportunities + planned experiments (batching, quantize, prefixing)
7) Renewal health summary: usage vs committed, renewal probability, suggested commercial moves
8) Action items & owners (30/60/90 day cadence)

Notes: include links to raw dashboards (Console) and attach sample payloads when discussing cacheability. Keep slides short; append full metric tables in backup deck.
renewal_tracker_fields: customer_id, primary_contact, contract_end_date, current_arr, committed_capacity, trailing_90d_usage, renewal_probability_percent, renewal_stage (early/engaged/negotiation/closed-won/lost), main_risks, open_action_items, last_cs_touch_date, next_eng_touch, recommended_price_walk, promo_allowed (Y/N)
notes:
Open questions / TODOs: 1) Agree canonical measurement for latency (include or exclude network? recommendation: server-only by default). 2) Decide whether to show cost/token as USD/token or USD/1k tokens in public decks (we prefer /1k for legibility). 3) Get SRE to add explicit cache lookup counters per-tenant in Console (ticket referenced).

Quick links: Confluence draft (linked above), Jira CS-4321 = 'Redefine QBR KPIs', PR-210 in observability repo = 'add cache metrics export'.

Small personal note: this is optimized for churned or at-risk accounts — for large strategic accounts we should include model-level degradation diagnostics and Eng presence in QBR meeting.
